data.standardized_narrative: At 31 December 2015 the syndicate had opening gross claims outstanding of $446.119m (31 Dec 2014). Analysis of the gross claims development triangle shows adverse prior-year development of $31.612m (7.1% of opening reserves), i.e. a strengthening of reserves. The movement reflects adverse development and large individual losses and an increase in IBNR across several older underwriting years, driven particularly by large loss development in energy and aviation-related accounts and reserve deterioration in long-tail specialty classes (professional indemnity/design & construction).
raw_causal_phrases: Net claims incurred of $211.4m (2014: $194.0m) increased modestly due to a number of new large losses experienced in June in particular.

The movement in the net provision for claims includes a release of $6,284,000 in respect of claims outstanding at the previous year end (2014: release $7,492,000). The release comprises net claim reductions including the change in claims incurred but not reported ('IBNR').
In particular the energy portfolio experienced the highest frequency of these risk losses.
In a number of cases these results were triggered by one off late claims notifications rather than any systemic issues arising within the lines of business themselves.
Losses included some that hit the headlines such as the PEMEX oil rig fire and the Germanwings and Shoreham Air Show aviation disasters.
data.data_quality_notes: Prior-year development was calculated from the gross claims development triangle (notes) because the movement note in the accounts quotes only net releases. All amounts are presented in the report's native currency (USD). The triangle values are presented in the accounts in $000; prior-year development was summed and converted to millions. Some line-of-business reserve movements are inferred from narrative rather than explicitly quantified. No RITC adjustment was identified in the technical reserves notes.
